oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty Alert: continuous-batching-latency-spike in prod (p1) — tail latency > 2s at high qps, error rate up 3x. root_ts=2150004321
oncall-bot: Incident channel auto-created: #incident-cb-jitter-2150004321
Alex W: acked. i'm on it, checking recent deploys and batch config.
Maria L: looking at graphs now — 99th latency spike aligns with increased concurrency ~10:12 UTC. KV cache evictions also spiked.
Kevin T: logs show microbatch sizes jumping from 4->32 under load. looks like batch-window heuristics mis-fired due to request fan-in.
Priya S: adding preliminary impact: 6 customers showing slow requests, one internal e2e failing. no elevated 5xx yet.
Alex W: digging into runtime metrics: continuous_batch.window_ms jumped from 10 -> 50ms under burst; that made microbatch combine too many inflight reqs. suspect jitter in arrival times amplified by prefix caching pressures.
Maria L: can we temporarily force fallback to fixed microbatch sizing? i can patch the autoscaler -> batching policy to cap microbatch at 8.
Kevin T: agree. quick mitigation: set `batching.max_microbatch_size=8` and `batching.window_ms=15` for the cb pool serving default model.
Priya S: +1. will also enable more aggressive kv-cache ttl to avoid cascading evictions: `kvcache.dynamic_ttl_ratio=0.25`
Alex W: prepping a hotpatch — applying to canary pool first. command:
```
# k8s patch for cb-config
kubectl -n inference patch configmap cb-config --patch '{"data":{"max_microbatch_size":"8","window_ms":"15"}}'
kubectl rollout restart deploy/cb-runtime-canary
```
Maria L: canary looks good so far (5m). tail latency back to normal. no errors.
pagerduty: Escalation: on-call acknowledged by Alex W. Next step: if canary stable for 10m, roll to prod pools.
Kevin T: rolling to prod now — using staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
Alex W: rolling. monitoring dashboard: qps steady, 95/99 back to baseline. kv-cache evictions trending down.
Priya S: posting brief customer impact note to #customer-impact: some users saw delays ~1-2s for 10m window; no data loss, no 5xx.
Maria L: follow-up root cause hypothesis: under high concurrency, arrival jitter + increased window_ms caused microbatch sizes to blow up which saturated KV cache IO and caused eviction storms -> higher lookup latencies -> backpressure and more batching.
Kevin T: action items:
- revert batching heuristic that increases window_ms aggressively under transient load (PR queued)
- add safety cap in runtime: `max_microbatch_size_soft=12`
- add metric alert for microbatch_size > 16 sustained 1m
- run chaos test for arrival jitter patterns
Alex W: tagging owners: @Maria L for rollout verification, @Kevin T for runtime PR, @Priya S for customer comms and post-incident notes.
oncall-bot: Handoff in 45m to next on-call (Priya S) — please summarize state in #incidents.
Priya S: summary saved to incident timeline. will take next shift and follow up on the PRs.
Alex W: closing mitigation: hotpatch rolled, metrics stable, no further pager. leaving notes for postmortem. :thumbsup:
